heading: Compaction and bearing capacity
text: Soil compaction increases dry density and reduces void ratio. A well compacted subgrade carries more load before shear failure occurs.

heading: Proctor test
text: The standard Proctor test establishes the maximum dry density and the optimum moisture content for a given soil. Compaction in the field is specified as a percentage of that maximum dry density.

heading: Why over-compaction is possible
text: Compacting beyond the optimum moisture content can reduce strength, because excess pore water carries load that the soil skeleton should carry.
